diagnostics.message: In the supplied graph, :resource.null_resource.file_permission is not ordered after :resource.local_file.private_ssh_key, so its local-exec chmod can run before the private-key file exists. key.tf already shows the appropriate explicit depends_on; retain it and ensure it is represented in the effective graph. Alternatively, use file-derived triggers to establish the ordering and rerun chmod when key content or the filename changes.

module.runner:data.template_file.gitlab_runner supplies the SSM parameter name from a local string rather than referencing module.runner:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. Consequently, the ASG can start user-data before Terraform creates the parameter that user-data manages. This can race token reads/writes or parameter creation. Populate the template variable from the managed parameter's name to order the downstream launch after parameter creation.

fix.expression:
{
  gitlab_runner_version                   = "${var.gitlab_runner_version}"
  docker_machine_version                  = "${var.docker_machine_version}"
  runners_config                          = "${data.template_file.runners.rendered}"
  runners_executor                        = "${var.runners_executor}"
  pre_install                             = "${var.userdata_pre_install}"
  post_install                            = "${var.userdata_post_install}"
  runners_gitlab_url                      = "${var.runners_gitlab_url}"
  runners_token                           = "${var.runners_token}"
  secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key = "${aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token.name}"
  secure_parameter_store_region           = "${var.aws_region}"
  gitlab_runner_registration_token        = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["registration_token"]}"
  giltab_runner_description               = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["description"]}"
  gitlab_runner_tag_list                  = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["tag_list"]}"
  gitlab_runner_locked_to_project         = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["locked_to_project"]}"
  gitlab_runner_run_untagged              = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["run_untagged"]}"
  gitlab_runner_maximum_timeout           = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["maximum_timeout"]}"
}

diagnostics.message: module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance launches a runner immediately (desired_capacity = 1), but its instance-profile reference only waits for the role/profile, not module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy. The runner can start accepting jobs before it has permission to provision Docker Machine workers. Order ASG creation after this attachment; ordering does not by itself eliminate IAM propagation delays.

module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance has no dependency on module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance. The runner can start handling builds before its cache-access policy is attached, causing initial cache operations to fail. Wait for this attachment before launching the runner.

When service-linked-role creation is enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role. Otherwise the runner can attempt to provision Spot workers before receiving the permission intended to create the required service-linked role in an account where it does not yet exist.

When token management is enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can execute its token-management user-data before module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm grants the instance role SSM access. Referencing the instance profile does not wait for policy attachments. Order the ASG after this attachment to avoid bootstrap AccessDenied failures.

With CloudWatch logging enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start the logging agent before module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.instance installs its logging permissions. The role/profile dependency does not include this inline policy. Wait for the policy before launching instances to avoid initial logging authorization failures.

module.runner:data.template_file.logging identifies the logging environment using only var.environment, so the downstream runner launch does not wait for module.runner:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment. With logging enabled, the agent can start before its managed log group exists, causing failed initial writes or an auto-creation race with Terraform. Reference the managed group's name in the template variables while preserving the disabled-logging case.

For the configured docker+machine executor, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start accepting jobs before module.runner:resource.aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_ssh is installed. Its transitive dependency on the worker security group does not wait for standalone rules. Docker Machine needs SSH access to provision workers, so wait for this rule before starting the runner.

module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance is ordered after the worker security group but not module.runner:resource.aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_docker. With docker+machine, early jobs can create workers before inbound Docker API access on port 2376 is available. Order runner startup after this standalone rule.

module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start provisioning Docker Machine workers before module.runner:resource.aws_security_group_rule.out_all grants their security group outbound connectivity. Referencing the group itself does not wait for this standalone egress rule. Wait for the rule before starting the runner so early worker bootstrap and image downloads have outbound access.
